<Rep. Terri A. Sewell>: I would like to give my sincere thanks to Chairman Smith and Ranking Member Neal for keeping the committee focused on AGOA reauthorization. As many of you know, years ago I made a promise to our former chairman Charlie Rangel that I would take on the mantle of preserving and protecting the AGOA program, and I know that he would be pleased that we are taking action today to reauthorize the program, even while there is so much instability in our current trade policy.
Over the last few years, I have met directly with AGOA country leaders, civil society groups, and the business community about the importance of the AGOA program. I was also honored to join Chairman Smith on the AGOA Codel last year when we visited Madagascar, Mauritius, and Benin.
What I've learned is that our AGOA partners truly value their partnership with the United States, and that our trade policies have the power to shape outcomes around the globe.
Economic growth is accelerating on the African continent, and population is expected to reach 2.5 billion by 2050. The region will become an economic powerhouse with a young workforce that will be exposed to emerging technologies that have the power to expedite growth. It is in America's interest to strengthen our ties with the region and deepen our trade relations.
However, AGOA is about more than tariff rates, quotas, or trade deficits. Passing this bill demonstrates that this committee is committed to our broad relationship with Africa. But more importantly, this bill sends a message that President Trump's horrible rhetoric toward many African countries is not an accurate reflection of America's values and priorities. Countries like South Africa and Nigeria have been recent targets of President Trump's racist and baseless attacks, but I am proud that this committee is taking truly bipartisan action to show that America will not turn its back on Africa. AGOA countries are our parters and deserve the dignity and respect that our other allies receive.
To be clear, AGOA isn't just a CBC priority. It has been a decades long bipartisan priority, and it stands as a proud example of Congress's commitment to deepening trust, stability, and shared prosperity with our AGOA allies.
I strongly support this 3-year reauthorization of the program. Moreover, during this extension, I hope that we can continue our bipartisan efforts to modernize the program. I believe we are making real progress on provisions that would strengthen enforcement, improve congressional oversight, strengthen critical mineral supply chains, improve utilization, and establish a smooth graduation path that encourages economic development.
Again, I want to give my sincere thanks to both Chairman Smith and Ranking Member Neal for making AGOA a bipartisan priority for this committee, and I strongly urge all my colleagues to vote for this bill and send a signal to our African allies that leaders in Congress respect and value our continued partnership.
Terri A. Sewell.
